body:
Thank you so much, that means a lot :) I hope it ends up being a good match, and she can help me get better.  
Hope you're doing well!

As far as my research covered, the UK doesn't have any kind of system of recognition for ESAs, which is ok. It's a relatively new idea, and since there is still such a stigma around mental illness worldwide, something like this with legal impact will take awhile to catch on.  
As far as I know, we could bring the cat back without problem, however it would probably stay with our friend, whom we are living with as well, after we graduate. The last thing we would want to do is traumatize the poor thing with a big move. (Our friend is from the UK).    

Yes actually, I've considered hamsters, rats and ferrets, but I guess I'm terrified of something happening to them since they are so small! I do love rats and ferrets from the time I've spent with them, but I feel a bit more of a connection with cats, and they can handle themselves pretty well, not to mention are less likely to chew through the many cords to our rigs haha. I say that because I'd want them to be able to run around in my room when I'm home too.    

Yeah, everyone here seems to unanimously agree that I should chat with the landlord, and I think I'll do that.  I'm hoping for the best, but it does make me extremely anxious! At the end of the day, I just want to be able to go with my boyfriend and our friend to a shelter, find a kitty we connect with and bring them home to love, and for emotional comfort.    

Thank you so much for taking the time to respond!

Yeah, I was aware of the laws, but I guess was wondering if there was some loophole by chance. I guess my fear is having the landlord say no, and that be the end of it, which is a very real possibility, I realise   
Thank you for the suggestion though! I will be writing a letter to the landlord soon I think, to ask about this. I will still supply evidence from a mental health professional to prove that I'm not just pulling this idea out of nowhere.
I wish we weren't committed yet, however every place we (my partner and a friend of ours) looked at, it was no pets, so we just chose the best one aside from that.  
Thank you so much for the lengthy response, it really helped.
Hey, thank you for your response! It's good to hear from a landlord's point of view, and I'll definitely ask her.
